summary.one_liner: HolmesGPT is an open-source AI agent that investigates production incidents and finds root causes across Kubernetes, VMs, cloud providers, databases, and SaaS tools; it is a CNCF sandbox project.
summary.what_it_does: HolmesGPT runs an agentic loop that queries live observability data from multiple sources to identify root causes of incidents. It ships with built-in toolsets (called data sources) for systems including Prometheus, Grafana, Datadog, Loki, Kubernetes, Helm, ArgoCD, AWS, Azure, GCP, GitHub, GitLab, Jira-related integrations, and many SQL and NoSQL databases, and users can add their own, including any REST API. It can pull alerts from AlertManager, PagerDuty, OpsGenie, or Jira and write findings back to the source or to Slack or Microsoft Teams (Slack and Teams via Robusta). An operator mode runs in Kubernetes in the background, runs scheduled health checks against connected data sources, and can message findings in Slack; with the GitHub integration it can open PRs. The README states the agent has read-only access and respects RBAC.
use_cases: investigate production incidents and find root causes
triage Prometheus or AlertManager alerts automatically
run scheduled health checks on services and deployments
troubleshoot Kubernetes pods, events, and Helm releases
query logs and metrics across Datadog, Grafana, Loki, or Splunk during an outage
post incident analysis to Slack, Jira, or PagerDuty
how_to_run: Read the installation documentation linked from the README (docs site)
Configure an LLM provider API key as described in the LLM Providers documentation
Enable the data source toolsets you need (e.g. Prometheus, Kubernetes)
Run interactive mode to ask questions and follow-ups
Optionally deploy operator mode in Kubernetes for background monitoring
stack: LLMs (OpenAI, Anthropic, Azure, Bedrock, Gemini, and others)
notable: Operator mode that monitors in the background and can open GitHub PRs with fixes
Built-in toolsets for dozens of observability, cloud, and database systems, plus custom REST API access
Memory-safe handling of large observability payloads, including per-tool memory limits and output budgeting
Bidirectional alert integrations that fetch alerts and write findings back
Works without Kubernetes, including on VMs, bare metal, and cloud services
caveats: Installation details, LLM provider setup, and usage guides are in external docs, not the README itself
Some integrations are only available through the HolmesGPT CLI (PagerDuty, OpsGenie, Jira, GitHub) or via Robusta (Slack, Teams)
Several toolsets are marked MCP and rely on hosted or external MCP servers
keywords: find why my service is down
